newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Media body disturbed by Belgian police TV raid.
newsitem.headline: Media body disturbed by Belgian police TV raid.

text.p: A raid by Belgian police on a Kurdish-language television station in Brussels was a grave violation of the rights of the media, the International Press Institute (IPI) said on Thursday.

The Vienna-based IPI, a network of editors and publishers representing media in 88 countries, said in a letter to Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene that it was deeply disturbed by the raid on the office of MED-TV on September 18.
"We understand that all occupants of the building were handcuffed and questioned for several hours," the IPI said in the letter.
Police confiscated various items, including computers and archive material, and closed down the licensed television station, forcing it to stop broadcasting, the IPI added.

"The IPI regards this action as a grave violation of the right to "seek, receive and impart information and ideas through any media regardless of frontiers' as guaranteed by article 19 of the United Nations Universal Declaration of Human Rights," it said.
Belgian media reported at the time that police believed the television network may have had links with the banned Kurdish PKK party.
